newsitem.title: ZAIRE: France should let Mobutu use Concorde, say rebels.
newsitem.headline: France should let Mobutu use Concorde, say rebels.

text.p: France should let ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko use a supersonic Concorde airliner if he is too sick to take a normal flight to talks in South Africa, anti-Mobutu rebels said on Thursday.

"If Mr Mobutu has difficulties in moving around then I believe it's time for France, which is the friend of Mr Mobutu, to put a Concorde at his disposal to permit him a quick trip to Pretoria," rebel information minister Raphael N'genda told reporters in Lubumbashi, the rebels' temporary headquarters.

Mobutu, sick with prostate cancer, has said he is too ill to fly to South Africa for talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, which the rebels say must result in his agreement to step down and transfer power to their alliance.
"We want them to take place in South Africa...we don't see why we need to look for another country. South Africa has made a great deal of effort to bring the two parties together."
South Africa said United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun would return to South Africa on Thursday to settle a date and venue for the Mobutu-Kabila meeting.
Kabila has rejected meeting Mobutu in Brazzaville, a ferry- boat ride across the Zaire river from the Zaire capital Kinshasa. Mobutu appears reluctant to go to Lubumbashi.
